issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int, boolean) while the problem statement (tasks and UML) and the solution both specify addGuestStudents(int). This parameter mismatch will confuse students and cause tests or expected usage (single-argument method) to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) so it matches the problem statement and the solution. If the boolean validation parameter is intended, update the problem statement and solution to document and use the two-parameter signature consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect an addGuestStudents(int) method (single int parameter), but the template defines addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with an extra boolean parameter. This creates a naming/signature mismatch for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students) and will confuse students about the required method signature and how to implement or call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } (remove the boolean validateInput parameter) so all artifacts refer to the same method signature and students have a consistent target to implement.
